ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: Held at 3, but the evidence base under it changed and the rationale is rewritten rather than inherited. The primary candidate is still carried by src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-ATE F1=0.6388 for GPT-4-turbo vs ~71-72% on knowledge-recall CTI-MCQ/CTI-RCM) and src-0005 (CyberSOCEval; test-time-scaling gains do not transfer to cybersecurity reasoning, benchmark 'far from saturating'). NEW AND UNCLAIMED: src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval, Mar 2026) is a third independent source measuring the same sub-task on real production CTI material, reporting MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (GPT-4o FT), 0.1771/0.1414 (GPT-4o-mini FT) -- far below CTIBench's 0.6388 F1 ceiling. This is NOT a contradiction: different benchmark, different corpus, and real-world material being harder than a curated benchmark is the expected direction, so no ctr entry was opened. It is genuine third-source corroboration of the direction of the claim, and it bears on two of the issue's three open_questions -- [0] (does the 0.64 ceiling generalize to newer models) is partly answered, since 2026-era GPT-4o/o3-mini are still nowhere near solving the task on real material; [2] (does ATT&CK-specific fine-tuning close the gap) gets its first direct evidence and the answer points the wrong way, since fine-tuned GPT-4o (0.2387/0.1846) scores BELOW zero-shot GPT-4o (0.2787/0.2270), echoing src-0001's finding that fine-tuning can degrade CTI performance. NOT raised to 4, for three stingy reasons: (a) src-0007 is cited here by T4 only -- the graph's candidate_resolutions for this issue still list evidence [src-0002, src-0005] and no cycle has attached it, so the state does not yet record this as a three-source claim (a T2 or T3 must attach it properly; flagged as carry-forward); (b) open_question[1] (human-analyst baseline F1) remains wholly unaddressed, so we still cannot say whether 0.64 is near or far from human performance, which is the counterargument that matters most for level 4; (c) src-0005's own recorded limitation -- no per-model numeric scores were ever captured, and cycle 9's G2 pass confirmed its claims in substance but explicitly NOT verbatim -- means one of the two attached sources is the weakest-verified in the base. No open contradiction on this issue, so no g3 demotion applies.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 2. This is the first cycle in which the g3 contradiction gate has ever fired in this project, and the arithmetic is stated separately so it is auditable. WHICH GATE READING I APPLIED, AND WHY: prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 describes a SUBTRACTION (lose gates.g3_contradiction_demotion = 2 points, floor 0); scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 implements a CEILING (error only if score > scale_max - demotion = 3). I applied the CEILING reading, and not merely because it is what the validator enforces. The rubric's levels are not points on an arithmetic scale, they are definitions of states: level 0 means 'no candidate resolutions' and level 1 means 'no supported resolution'. This issue has three candidate_resolutions, two of them with status supported. Any subtraction that lands on 0 or 1 therefore assigns a label that is flatly false of the issue, which is worse than useless to the weakest-link selector that reads these numbers. The ceiling reading achieves what the gate is for -- an unresolved conflict blocks the top of the scale -- without corrupting the meaning of the bottom of it. I record that the two specifications genuinely disagree and that T4 has no standing to reconcile them; that is carried forward for a cycle that does. THE ARITHMETIC: pre-demotion score on the merits = 2. Post-demotion = 2 (ceiling of 3 is not binding). I did NOT take pre-demotion to be 3, and this is where I part company with the framing handed to me by cycle 9's queue entry, which asserted that two independent sources meet 'the rubric's stated bar for 3'. The rubric's bar is that the PRIMARY CANDIDATE be supported by >=2 independent sources, not that the issue accumulate 2 sources. Per-candidate, the state is: candidate 1 (LANCE 97.6% F1) evidence [src-0003] alone; candidate 2 (vanilla-LLM precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1310 expert-annotated IoCs) evidence [src-0007] alone; candidate 3, the scaffolding-not-the-model synthesis, is the only one citing multiple sources (src-0003 + src-0007 + src-0008) and cycle 9 deliberately gave it status 'proposed', not 'supported', precisely because no source tests it. Two single-source candidates plus one proposed synthesis is the textbook shape of a level 2. And the substantive point behind the formalism is the same one: src-0003 and src-0007 do not jointly support one claim, they pull in opposite directions on magnitude -- a bare LLM at 0.82-0.88 precision lands at or below the 86% VirusTotal@threshold=1 baseline that src-0003 presents as the tool LANCE beats. Sources that leave a reader with opposite impressions are not corroboration; that is exactly why ctr-0001 exists. WHAT I ENGAGED ON THE OTHER SIDE: ctr-0001 itself names three confounds (SYSTEM -- LANCE is regex+LLM+human-validation while src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs'; METRIC -- 97.6% is F1 while 0.82-0.88 are precision with no recall or F1 reported anywhere for that task; CORPUS -- 50 public threat reports vs an unnamed company's internal workflow) and states that if the SYSTEM confound is confirmed the contradiction should be closed and folded into candidate 3. That is a real possibility and it is why I did not treat the conflict as a reason to score BELOW 2 either. The honest position is that the issue is better evidenced than it was at cycle 4 and simultaneously less settled, and 2 is the number that says so. Note the sequencing consequence: under the subtraction reading this issue would now be the graph's unique weakest link at 1 and would monopolise T5; under the ceiling reading it sits in a three-way tie at 2 with an attempt penalty against it (attempts [9], within the last 5 cycles). I flag that the gate reading changes the research agenda, not just a number.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: Held at 2. Both candidate_resolutions still cite evidence [src-0001] only; the cycle-3 candidate sharpens the cycle-2 one using the SAME source, so two candidates are not two sources. Cycle 7's G2 pass re-fetched https://arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and re-confirmed the model identities (gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, mistral-large-2), the 350-report set, the 10-re-prompt bootstrapped-CI method (max CI width 0.02 extraction vs 0.06 generation) and all ten Table-6 gpt4o ECE/Brier values -- high confidence in one source is still single-source support. Checked the two cycle-9 sources for corroboration and rejected both: src-0007 reports precision/recall only, with no repeated-query consistency measure and no ECE/Brier anywhere; src-0008 measures a code-analysis task, not CTI reasoning. WORTH RECORDING FROM THIS CYCLE'S G2 PULL, but deliberately NOT scored on: src-0008's Table 6 and Table 7, which I pulled verbatim, contain an abstention/overconfidence pattern that is at least adjacent to this issue -- Cohere emitted 625 'Don't Know' responses and Gemini emitted 0, and Gemini is also the model with by far the highest hallucination rate (4.8%, vs Anthropic 0.11%, ChatGPT 0.23%, Grok 0%, Cohere 0%). A model that never abstains being the model that most often invents an indicator is the overconfidence phenomenon this issue is about, but it is measured on JavaScript source code rather than CTI material, it is not attached to any candidate_resolution, and one cross-model correlation on n=5 vendors is not evidence of a mechanism. It is logged as a candidate for a T2/T3 to attach or dismiss, not as a second source. All four open_questions remain unaddressed. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: Held at 3, unchanged in substance from cycle 7 and re-checked against the two sources added in cycle 9. The primary candidate rests on 2 genuinely independent sources, both attached: src-0002 (CTIBench CTI-TAA over 50 real reports; GPT-4-turbo 86% plausible vs 52% correct, Gemini-1.5 74% vs 38%) and src-0004 (Heise/Der Spiegel on ENISA's 2025 Threat Landscape reports; APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' misattribution published in production). An academic benchmark plus investigative reporting on a production incident is real independence, which is what distinguishes this issue from the single-source 2s. Checked whether cycle 9's additions move it: they do not. src-0007 measures IoC extraction, TTP identification and triage, but reports no plausible-vs-correct attribution split and no threat-actor attribution task; src-0008 is a code-analysis benchmark. Not raised to 4: open_question[2] -- whether src-0004's naming-convention hallucination is the same phenomenon as src-0002's quantified plausible/correct gap or a distinct citation/naming-fabrication sub-type -- is the explicit alternative explanation for the pair, and it has been articulated since cycle 2 without ever being argued either way. Level 4 requires counterarguments explicitly addressed, not merely listed. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: Held at 3, and I considered moving it in BOTH directions before holding. What changed: src-0007 is a fourth WITHIN-study demonstration of the narrow claim (same team, same corpus, same four models, same Table 4: IoC extraction precision 0.82-0.88 vs TTP identification 0.2787/0.2270 for GPT-4o), joining src-0006, src-0002 and src-0001. The narrow claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- is now about as well-evidenced as anything in this graph. Case for raising to 4, rejected: the issue as TITLED and as scoped by its own open_questions is not the narrow claim, it is the specific ordinal axis 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation', and that axis did not get more settled this cycle, it got more CONTESTED. src-0007's Table 4 cuts IN FAVOUR of the axis (extraction cleanly beats mapping in one controlled setting), while src-0006's Table 5 cuts against it by marking failure subtypes as spanning all four pipeline stages (e.g. 'Co-mention bias (Type 1.1) -- stages 1234', re-confirmed live by cycle 8's G2 pass). Cycle 7's and cycle 8's rationales read this one-sidedly against the axis; that reading is no longer tenable and I am not inheriting it. Case for LOWERING, also rejected: the two are not strictly contradictory and I explicitly declined to open a contradiction entry for them, because src-0006's claim is about where failure MECHANISMS occur and src-0007's is about where performance LEVELS differ -- the same mechanism can operate at every stage while its impact is far larger on mapping than on extraction. Both can be true, and cycle 8's near-miss on a spurious contradiction is the standing reminder not to manufacture one from an apparent tension. So: narrow claim strengthened to roughly a 4-source footing, distinguishing axis now actively disputed by two sources instead of doubted by one, and a single score is still averaging them. Scored on the axis alone this issue is a 1-2; scored on the narrow claim alone, 3 (arguably 4 once the counterargument is addressed rather than merely noted). 3 is the stingy resultant. THIS IS THE FOURTH CONSECUTIVE CYCLE (7, 8, 9, 10) RECOMMENDING THE SPLIT, and the split is now the single highest-value structural change available to the graph, because it is the only thing that would let either half be scored honestly. T4 has no standing to restructure; only a T2 does.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: Held at 2. Sole candidate's evidence is src-0004 alone (Heise/Der Spiegel on ENISA); single-source support caps this at 2 regardless of how well verified that source is, and it is well verified -- cycle 4's G2 pass re-fetched the URL and confirmed the 26-of-492 incorrect-footnote figure, the APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' fingerprint, and ENISA's 'human errors' response permitting AI for 'minor editorial revisions'. Neither cycle-9 source touches this issue: src-0007 and src-0008 are both benchmarks, and no source in the base other than src-0004 documents a production/publication incident at a named institution. Note for the selector: this is now the ONLY issue in the graph with no new evidence since cycle 1, a nine-cycle drought, and it has never been the target of a T1 or T3. That is not a reason to change the score, but it is the reason its score has not moved. Level 4 is additionally blocked by scope rather than by evidence volume -- open_question[0] asks for an industry base rate across CTI publishers, and the candidate itself claims existence but explicitly not frequency, so even a second incident report would establish a second data point rather than a rate. No open contradiction, so no g3 demotion.
